title: Average Causal Effect Estimation in DAGs with Hidden Variables: Beyond Back-Door and Front-Door Criteria
abstract: arXiv:2409.03962v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The identification theory for causal effects in directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) with hidden variables is well established, but methods for estimation and inference beyond the g-formula remain less developed. Previous studies have introduced influence-function-based estimators for broad classes of identifiable effects. When implemented through the observed-data density factorization, these estimators can require conditional density estimation and numerical integration, which can be statistically challenging and computationally demanding for continuous or multivariate variables. Prior work on related causal functionals has used sequential regressions and Bayes-rule representations of density ratios to avoid these requirements. translated_title: 含隐变量DAG中的平均因果效应估计：超越后门与前门准则
translated_abstract: 具有隐变量的有向无环图（DAG）中因果效应的识别理论已经相当成熟，但超越g-公式的估计与推断方法仍发展不足。以往研究已针对广泛类别的可识别效应引入了基于影响函数的估计量。当通过观测数据密度分解来实现这些估计量时，往往需要进行条件密度估计和数值积分，这对于连续变量或多变量而言在统计上具有挑战性且计算代价高昂。此前关于相关因果泛函的研究采用了序贯回归和密度比的贝叶斯法则表示来避免这些需求。基于已有的识别理论与影响函数结果，我们将这些重参数化明确应用于在处理原始可固定性、Tian和Pearl的充要条件下所识别的效应……
tldr: 该论文针对含隐变量DAG中超越后门与前门准则的可识别因果效应，提出了基于序贯回归和贝叶斯法则重参数化的估计方法，从而避免了条件密度估计与数值积分带来的统计和计算难题。
en_tdlr: This paper provides explicit reparameterizations via sequential regressions and Bayes-rule representations of density ratios for estimating identifiable causal effects in DAGs with hidden variables beyond back-door and front-door criteria, avoiding the statistical and computational challenges of conditional density estimation and numerical integration.
